selection_basis: The first four actionable records emitted by the canonical review queue after claim cleanup batch eight completed and before any batch-nine rewrite was applied.

observed_initial_queue.blocked_reason: The higher-priority preview consisted of sensitive or restricted records requiring actual-source and safety review rather than automatic practical rewriting.

guardrail: This batch preserves only bounded operational procedures. It removes inherited unsupported quantitative, first-party, psychological, health-adjacent and performance claims, adds no source and promotes no entry to reviewed.

entries.decision: Remove fabricated project outcomes, psychological mechanism claims, universal timing and sample rules, health and emotional examples, and assumptions about other people's motives or capacities. Preserve a decision-context check: state what changed, identify concrete constraints and stakeholders, separate verified facts from assumptions, and choose a reversible next step when important context remains unknown.

Remove fabricated editing and publication outcomes, invented user tests, fixed word-count menus, pseudo-precise timing and unsupported claims about platform expectations. Preserve a pre-draft brief that names the primary reader, publication surface, purpose, required constraints and verification needs before the writer chooses structure and tone.

Remove unsupported language-learning effects, fabricated classroom and pilot outcomes, rigid phrase counts and repetition schedules, physiological or anxiety claims, and pharmacy or dosage scenarios. Preserve a low-risk scenario rehearsal: choose a real interaction, prepare the minimum useful phrases plus a repair phrase, rehearse both sides, try the interaction when appropriate, and update the phrase set from what was actually difficult.

Remove therapy and physiological framing, medical and family-health examples, fabricated completion outcomes, fixed concern counts, timing prescriptions and claims about attention or emotional release. Preserve an action-allocation workflow: separate outcomes you can directly produce from dependencies you can only influence or observe, choose one controllable next action, and define how to revisit waiting items.
